workflow: Round 17 (s12) won the authority trap at scale but exposed a residual: method Haiku surfaced the spec-vs-test conflict 3/3, yet only 1/3 took the ideal action (fix the wrong test); the other 2/3 flagged the contradiction but still edited the contractual code, reading 'fix the code' as authority. This is the same residual s2 documented at single-file scale, and it is a real action gap, not just an observability gap. Mitigation, following the round-13 pattern (forced artifact at the decision point): strengthen the Step 4.1 intent gate so that when the spec sides with the current code against a failing check, the required action is to fix the CHECK, not the code, with a forced report line: 'RESOLUTION: spec agrees with the code; the failing check is wrong; fixing the check, not the code.' A/B: 4 method-Haiku runs on the mitigated SKILL vs the round-17 method arm as baseline (same s12 fixture, unmitigated SKILL, 1/3 ideal). Grading is MECHANICAL: fix_location (test_corrected = ideal, rate_changed = took the trap) by diff, both determined by which file changed.

result.resolution_line_emitted: 2/4 (mit-1, mit-3 verbatim; mit-2 ideal action without the literal line)

ideal: fixed the test citing the README authority clause; no literal RESOLUTION line
ideal: fixed the test, RESOLUTION line present

interpretation: The authority-action gate works. It lifted the ideal-action rate from 1/3 to 3/4 by converting the s2/s12 residual (surface-but-still-edit) into fix-the-right-side, exactly as the round-13 artifact gate converted the EMBEDDED dropout. The forced RESOLUTION line is the mechanism: two runs emitted it verbatim and fixed the test; a third took the ideal action reasoning from the README authority clause without the literal line. The one residual run (mit-4) still edited the code, so the gate does not fully close the gap at the bottom tier, the same ceiling every Haiku-tier mitigation in this log hits. But raising a documented residual from 33% to 75% on a real action gap is a genuine lift, measured trap-first (the rule shipped only after the A/B showed it helps).
limitations: n=4 mitigated vs n=3 baseline, one fixture, Haiku only, mechanical scoring. Directional, not a significance claim. The residual is reduced, not eliminated; mit-4 shows the bottom-tier ceiling persists. Shipped in SKILL + AGENTS with the sync guard extended to pin the RESOLUTION phrase.
